In East Uusimaa, giving eligible breast patients 5 instead of 15 sessions would save about 28 patients 282 round trips and 410 road hours yearly; no municipality lies beyond the 100 km commuting threshold, so nights away are few [S34, S57, S60].

1. Radiation oncology heads at HUS, Kotka and Lahti could evaluate a single 8 Gy session as default for uncomplicated painful bone metastases (equal pain relief, more retreatment) [S31, S30]. Askola (66 km from Helsinki): expected round trips 2.4 instead of 6.2 [S34, S57, S60]. HUS publicly mentions pain relief for spread cancer but no schedule [S36]. First step within 30 days: draft it with palliative care [S32]. Goal 3 indicator: national targets and key effectiveness indicators defined for agreed cancers [S61].

2. The breast team lead could evaluate 5 sessions as default for eligible patients (whole breast or chest wall, no nodal radiotherapy), naming distance as a reason; it is non-inferior to 15 [S9, S15]. Askola: 6 round trips instead of 16; county: 282 machine sessions freed yearly [S34, S57, S60]. First step within 30 days: audit eligible patients' schedules [S15]. Goal 3 indicator: patients receive treatment within target times [S25, S24].

3. The cancer quality lead could publish schedule mix and radiotherapy use by distance band yearly [S21, S27]. First step within 30 days: request counts by home municipality from the treating units [S26]. Goal 3 indicator: regional differences in treatment are available and used to steer services [S26].

Limitations: patients are allocated by population, distances run from municipality centres, and schedule mix is assumed [S57, S59, S60].
